newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products end steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products end steady to firm.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products ended steady to higher on Tuesday, traders said.
High and low sulphur fuel oil held steady with swaps and stable futures. Traders said recent sales of high sulphur fuel to the Far and Middle East were also fundamentally supportive.
"Sentiment is a touch firmer today even if there haven't been a lot of offers," said one buyer.
Both products were said to be in adequate supply, although some traders said it was becoming difficult to find prompt high sulphur material to fill ships heading east.
High sulphur fob stems valued around $78 with low sulphur liftings around $93 a tonne.
Gasoline was steady. Traders said requirement into France, Italy and Spain appeared to have been covered ahead of a round of spring maintenance shutdowns.
Demand was reported out of Lebanon and Turkey but traders said the few cargoes available on the spot market did not conform to the required specifications.

A couple of refiners were heard offering mid octane material. "The trouble is the material on offer is mid octane spec and Turkey wants higher octane stuff, while Lebanon is looking for stuff with just one percent benzine content," said one trader.
On the naphtha front, traders said although key suppliers were dry, material could still be found.
Arbitraging Russian gas oil to Asia, particularly India, but also Singapore, remained the focus of attention.

Russian gas oil was firm around high cif quotes +$2-3 because of short-term tightness, while Italian spec was steady at cif high quotes +$3-4. But traders said interest for non-Russian heating oil was fairly minimal and the strength of Italian spec was essentially derived from the Russian rise.
